instruction.text: Select the adverb that makes the sentence less certain.

atoms.b: They could ((potentially)) win the premiership next year.
atoms.sound: They could potentially win the premiership next year.

instruction.text: Select the adverb that makes the sentence more certain.

atoms.b: He might ((possibly)) be the best candidate for the job.
atoms.sound: He might possibly be the best candidate for the job.

instruction.text: Select the adverb that makes the sentence more certain.

atoms.b: It is ((likely)) we will be late because of the traffic.
atoms.sound: It is likely we will be late because of the traffic.

instruction.text: Select the adverb that makes the sentence more certain.

atoms.b: There are ((definitely)) many more species in rainforests we haven’t discovered yet.
atoms.sound: There are definitely many more species in rainforests we haven’t discovered yet.

instruction.text: Look at the adverbs and order the sentences by likelihood, starting with the most likely.

atoms.text: If the weather is good, we will certainly have a picnic tomorrow.
If the weather is good, we will likely have a picnic tomorrow.
If the weather is good, maybe we will have a picnic tomorrow.

instruction.text: Look at the adverbs and order the sentences by likelihood, starting with the most likely.
Look at the degree of possibility and select an appropriate adverb.

atoms.b: We ((++definitely maybe)) will do a class play this year.
((++Maybe Probably)) we will do better next time.
((++Perhaps Certainly)) we will spot a dolphin while we’re at the beach this weekend.
We will ((certainly ++probably)) see some rare birds on our hike.
